goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:6 — Both new controller specs assert only `X < Admin::AdminController`, so they stay green if every action 500s — create/update/destroy, category assignment, and admin-only enforcement have zero coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new controller specs that only assert inheritance and do not exercise any controller behavior. `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` contains only `expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` mirrors that. Meanwhile, the PR introduces nontrivial actions in `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` (create/update/destroy plus `save_host` parameter handling and defaulting category_id) and `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb` (show/update and `fetch_embedding`). As written, these specs would remain green even if the actions raised errors or authorization/JSON behavior regressed, so the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a defect in runtime code.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:24 — category_id` is never validated to exist or to be non-read-restricted, so a host can be pointed at a private/secure category (or a bogus id) and `TopicEmbed.import` creates topics there with `skip_validations: true`, making the embedded comment threads inaccessible to the anonymous readers they were created for.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host the submitted `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` is assigned directly (only defaulting when blank) with no check that the category exists or is publicly readable; there’s also no FK constraint in the migration to prevent bogus IDs. That `category_id` is later used in `TopicEmbed.import` (`category: eh.try(:category_id)`) while `skip_validations: true` is set, so an allowed host can be configured to create embedded topics in a read-restricted/private category or with an invalid category reference, leading to inaccessible embed threads or incorrect behavior.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 — update` and `destroy` (line 15) use `where(id: ...).first` with no nil check, so an unknown or already-deleted id returns a 500 NoMethodError instead of a 404/error JSON body.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately call methods on the result (`save_host(host)` which does `host.host = ...`, and `host.destroy`). If the id is unknown or already deleted, `host` will be `nil`, causing a `NoMethodError` (500) rather than a controlled 404/error JSON response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — type.replace('_','-')` replaces only the first underscore, so the ADMIN_MODELS lookup will silently miss any future multi-underscore admin type and route it to `/` instead of `/admin/`; needs a global replace.

adjudication.rationale: In `basePath(store, type)`, the diff changes the admin-model check to `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-')) !== -1`. In JavaScript, `String#replace` without a regex replaces only the first underscore, so a hypothetical future admin model type with multiple underscores (e.g. `foo_bar_baz`) would become `foo-bar_baz` and fail to match an ADMIN_MODELS entry like `foo-bar-baz`, incorrectly falling back to `"/"` instead of `"/admin/"`. The diff doesn’t show any current multi-underscore admin types, so it’s not a demonstrated breakage now, but it is a specific, actionable robustness issue introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — execute(...)[0]['id']` raises IndexError when no `embed_category` site_settings row exists (the default case), so the migration aborts for nearly every install and the `category_id == 0` fallback is unreachable.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration unconditionally does `execute(...)[0]['id']` for the `embed_category` lookup. If that SELECT returns zero rows (e.g., no `site_settings` row named `embed_category`), `[0]` will be `nil` and `nil['id']` will raise, aborting the migration before the `category_id == 0` fallback can run. The finding’s exact exception type may be off (more likely NoMethodError than IndexError), but the crash condition is real from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5 — category_id` is `null: false` with no default, no FK and no index; the fallback can insert `-1` (the `uncategorized_category_id` default) or another id with no matching category, producing orphaned rows.

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `embeddable_hosts.category_id` as `null: false` but does not add an index or a foreign key constraint, and the model/controller code does not validate that the provided `category_id` actually exists (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` directly). That makes orphaned `embeddable_hosts` rows possible if an invalid ID is ever inserted/updated. However, the specific claim that the fallback can insert `-1` is not supported by the diff: the migration falls back to `uncategorized_category_id` (converted via `to_i`), not `-1`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9 — update` is identical to `show` and persists nothing, so the PUT endpoint and its fake OpenStruct `id: 'default'` resource are a stub abstraction.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` simply re-renders the same serialized `@embedding` OpenStruct as `show` and does not apply or persist any params (the OpenStruct is built in `fetch_embedding` with `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all...`). The diff also adds a PUT route (`put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`) and a client action (`admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` `saveChanges() { this.get('embedding').update({}); }`) implying an updatable resource, but there’s no server-side persistence behind it. This is a diff-grounded incompleteness/architecture concern rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect in the shown UI (hosts are persisted via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5 — saveChanges` is not referenced by any template and only calls the no-op embedding update endpoint - dead code.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`, the `saveChanges` action only does `this.get('embedding').update({});`. The only added template for this feature (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) wires up actions for `addHost` and `deleteHost` but does not reference `saveChanges` anywhere, so it is currently unused/dead code. Additionally, the corresponding Rails `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` just re-renders the serializer without persisting anything, making the call effectively a no-op even if it were invoked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:200 — hydrated || []` is unreachable dead code because `Array#map` always returns an array.

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js` plural branch, `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` will always produce an Array when it executes, and in JS even `[]` is truthy, so `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` will never use the `[]` fallback. This is a redundant expression (right-hand side effectively dead), but it doesn’t create broken behavior by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196 — the new _ids branch calls obj[k].map without checking it is an array and deletes the key even when no side-loaded collection exists, so a null/scalar *_ids value throws and a missing collection silently yields [undefined]

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural `_ids` handling (`if (m[2])`) unconditionally calls `obj[k].map(...)` (so `null`, `undefined`, or scalar `*_ids` values will throw), and it always deletes `obj[k]` while setting `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]` to the mapped results even if `_lookupSubType` can’t resolve any records from the side-loaded `root` (yielding an array of `undefined` entries and losing the original ids). This behavior is directly visible in the added branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:6 — Only asserts the class inherits from Admin::AdminController, so create/update/destroy, param handling, the uncategorized fallback, and staff authz are entirely untested and the spec would still pass if every action were deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial behavior in `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` (create/update/destroy, `save_host` param usage `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`/`[:category_id]`, uncategorized fallback via `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, and staff/login filters). The new spec `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` only asserts inheritance (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`) and would still pass even if the actions/filters/param handling were removed or broken, leaving the newly introduced controller behavior effectively untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:6 — Same inheritance-only assertion leaves show/update and EmbeddingSerializer output with zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new runtime behavior in `Admin::EmbeddingController` (`before_filter :fetch_embedding`, `show`/`update` rendering `EmbeddingSerializer` with embedded `embeddable_hosts`) and new serializers (`EmbeddingSerializer`, `EmbeddableHostSerializer`), but the added spec `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` only asserts inheritance (`Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController`) and does not exercise the `show`/`update` actions or verify the serialized JSON structure. This leaves the new endpoint/serialization logic effectively untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb:1 — File contents were swapped: the embeddable_host fabricator now lives in category_fabricator.rb and all category fabricators in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb; the suite still passes only because Fabrication loads every file under spec/fabricators regardless of name

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the fabricator definitions were effectively swapped: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (and no longer defines any category fabricators), while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:category)` and related category variants that used to live in `category_fabricator.rb`. This is confusing/misleading organization and could trip up developers/tools that assume fabricator files match their contents, even if Fabrication loads all files under `spec/fabricators` so the test suite still works.
